faq: Can you work from my design file?
Yes. Figma, Sketch, Adobe XD or plain images and wireframes all work. We match spacing, type and color closely, and flag anything in the design that would not work on a small screen.
React and Next.js are our focus here. For Vue, Svelte or Angular, tell us in the form and we confirm whether we can take it on before you order.
Do I need a back end already?
Not for Basic, where we build with sample data. For Standard and Premium we connect to your API. If no API exists yet, the back-end development service covers it.
Will it look the same on every device?
It will look right on each one, which is not always identical. We build layouts that adapt from phones to wide monitors and check them in Chrome, Safari and Firefox.

desc:
React and Next.js front-end development turns designs, a Figma file or rough sketches into fast, responsive screens people can use. Ecom Swift LLC builds clean components, connects them to your API and tests them across browsers and screen sizes.

## What is front-end development in React and Next.js?

Front-end development is the work of building everything a user sees and touches in a web app: layouts, buttons, forms, menus and the way they respond. React is a widely used library for building interfaces from small reusable pieces called components. Next.js is a framework built on React that adds routing, server rendering and tools for fast, search-friendly pages.

The front end talks to a back end through an API. It asks for data, shows it clearly and sends back whatever the user enters. Good front-end work makes that exchange feel instant and clear.

## Why screen quality decides how an app is judged

People judge software in seconds. A screen that shifts as it loads, a form that fails without explanation or a layout that breaks on a phone makes the whole product feel unfinished, even if the back end is excellent. Users rarely report these problems. They simply leave.

Good front-end work protects the investment you made in design and in the back end. It also keeps maintenance affordable, because well-organized components can be changed in one place instead of fixed screen by screen.

## How it affects usability and growth

Clear loading and error states tell users what is happening instead of leaving them guessing. Validation on forms catches typos before they become support requests. Responsive layouts let customers finish tasks on a phone, where many sessions begin.

With Next.js, pages can be rendered on the server, which helps content load quickly and be read by search engines. Fast, stable pages are easier to use and easier to find. The exact effect depends on your content and audience, but the foundations are all within the front end.

## What great front-end work includes

- Pixel-careful screens that follow your design, with sensible choices where it is silent.
- A library of reusable components for buttons, inputs, tables, modals and navigation.
- Responsive layouts for phone, tablet and desktop.
- Loading, empty and error states on every screen that fetches data.
- Forms with clear validation messages and accessible labels.
- Page routing and navigation that behave as users expect.
- A connection to your API with careful handling of failures.
- Testing in the main browsers, plus automated tests on important screens.
- Keyboard and screen reader support, checked against WCAG 2.1 AA on larger builds.
- Clean code in your repository, with notes for the next developer.

## What we do

We review your designs, flag gaps early and agree how each screen should behave. We then set up the project, build the shared components first and assemble the screens from them. Forms, routing and API calls are added, and everything is tested on real browsers and phone sizes.

The Basic package delivers a few polished screens with responsive layouts, reusable components and loading and error states. Standard adds more screens, validated forms, API connections, routing and testing in three browsers. Premium adds a larger set of screens, a shared design system, an accessibility pass, automated tests on key screens, a performance check and handover notes. Add-ons include extra screens, dark mode and a component library.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Share designs with real text and images, not only placeholders.
- Tell us what each button and form should do when it fails.
- Agree the API shape, or ask us to document what is needed.
- Review progress on a real phone and a real laptop.
- Keep fonts, spacing and colors consistent across screens.

**Avoid:**
- Sending designs for desktop only when most users are on phones.
- Leaving empty and error states undefined.
- Copying the same layout code into many screens.
- Loading large images and libraries that the page does not need.
- Changing the design after screens are built without re-checking the whole flow.

## Who it is for

This service suits a team with designs and no developer to build them, a founder whose back end is ready but whose interface is not, and an agency that needs reliable help with React or Next.js work. It also suits owners whose current screens are slow or hard to maintain.

## What we need from you

Send your designs or sketches, your brand assets, a link to your API or its documentation, and a list of the browsers your users rely on. We never need passwords. For repository and hosting access, you add us as a collaborator or developer user.
